name: Nuclino
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Maintain a fast linked team knowledge base with collections and simple boards

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 50 items across all workspaces; 3 canvases; 2 GB total storage

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited items/canvases; 30-day history; 10 GB storage/user; admin tools and publishing
tiers.notes: The live indexed official page exposes $6/user/month while the billing toggle advertises monthly and yearly; the exact no-commitment monthly price did not render, so $6 is stored as the annual-billed monthly equivalent.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited history; 20 GB/user; Sidekick AI, audit log, insights, SSO, security controls and custom publishing domain
tiers.notes: The exact no-commitment monthly price did not render; $10 is stored as the annual-billed monthly equivalent.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 50 items across all workspaces, 3 canvases and 2 GB total storage
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to 25% off); 14-day no-card Starter trial; exact no-commitment prices did not render
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every person in the team, including guests and read-only members, is a billable user on paid plans. New users are prorated. Teams over 100 users must contact sales.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Nuclino, maintain a fast linked team knowledge base with collections and simple boards. The hard boundary is real-time collaboration, hosted sync, permissions, and dependable search, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Maintain a fast linked team knowledge base with collections and simple boards, search notes instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: real-time collaboration, hosted sync, permissions, and dependable search
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Nuclino because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: BookStack
alternatives.desc: A wiki arranged like a bookshelf, which is either charming or compulsory.

facts.install: Fresh Ubuntu install script or manual PHP/MySQL setup
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, permissions, and settings in MySQL/MariaDB; uploaded images and files in the server filesystem or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its shelf/book/chapter hierarchy is much more rigid than Nuclino's free-form collections, linked graph, canvas and board views.
facts.setupBlocker: The official script expects a fresh Ubuntu host; manual installs require PHP extensions, a database, writable storage, mail, and TLS

alternatives.name: Docmost
alternatives.desc: A clean team wiki with a database bill instead of a seat bill.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, comments, and history in PostgreSQL; jobs/cache in Redis; attachments in a persistent local volume by default or S3/Azure Blob
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a strong document wiki, but its boards, visual graph and real-time product polish are less mature than Nuclino's tightly integrated workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, a strong APP_SECRET, database credentials, persistent volumes, and normally a domain, TLS reverse proxy, and SMTP

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.desc: A polished wiki, provided you are willing to become its part-time sysadmin.

facts.install: Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, or a Node.js package plus a supported database
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, authentication data, and history in the configured database; optional storage modules can mirror content and assets to Git, local disk, or cloud storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It provides a capable wiki but not Nuclino's lightweight canvas, graph and board workflow, and it asks someone to administer a database-backed server.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision a database and persistent volumes, then configure backups and a TLS reverse proxy for public use

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Nuclino in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: maintain a fast linked team knowledge base with collections and simple boards, search notes instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
